editorial.headline: Insurance Loss Assessment: Open Nationally, Unblocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: A claims-time specialist activity, open to foreign investment nationally and not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Insurance loss assessment is work undertaken when an insurance claim occurs. It covers the assessment of claims and/or consulting services concerning the insured object: the practical, informed appraisal required when a claimed loss must be evaluated. The activity is identified with the loss adjuster’s role at the point of claim, and is governed in accordance with the provisions of Indonesia’s Financial Services Authority.

The businesses registering this activity are therefore those built around claims assessment or advisory work on insured objects. Its permitted scale is notably broad: micro, small, medium and large enterprises may undertake it. That range matters because the work is defined by its function in the claims process, rather than by a single business size. Whether the undertaking is compact or substantial, the stated activity remains the assessment of insurance claims and related consultation on the insured object.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is open. Foreign ownership may reach 100%, under the PMA basis cited for the activity. In plain terms, the national record does not impose a foreign-equity cap below full ownership. That openness sits alongside a clear description of the business itself: this is not an abstract advisory label, but a claims-time activity focused on assessing claims and advising on the object that is insured.

Bali does not reverse that national position. The province’s permanent, island-wide PMA moratorium blocks activities carrying Low or Medium-Low risk, but this activity is marked as not blocked. The Bali record states that, at the large-enterprise scale, the OSS risk level is Medium-High/High, which is why it is not caught by that moratorium. The practical reading is straightforward: the activity is open nationally to full foreign ownership and remains unblocked for PMA registration in Bali.
